w: The evening assembly was celebrated as Yuva-Kishore day. Special programs were presented by the youth and teenage members of Satsang.
Swamishri blessed the participants of a Teachers Camp held in the mandir and 47 kishores who to please Swamishri, had prostrated their way from Botad to Sarangpur.

When Pramukh Swami Maharaj was going to his room for the night, teenagers from abroad who were travelling with him were standing there. All said in one voice, "We are all Swami's children, we will die for Swami."
On hearing this, Swamishri stopped and said, "Why die? Live for Swami instead!"
"Even if we live, it will be for you." Jignesh (Miami) expressed his resolve in line with Swamishri's words.
So Swamishri looked at the other teenagers and said, "What do you have to do?"
All said, "We have to work according to your command."
"What work?"
"Whatever work you say. We have to do your work," the teenagers answered naturally.

But Swamishri immediately said, "Where is there any work of mine? It is the work of Maharaj, Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj. That is what we all have to do. Even living in worldly life, we are to do that same work, and if by their command we become sadhus, we are still to do that same work."
Then he said, "All right. Thank you."
In this way, giving them a memory, he went to rest.

"Even if we live, it will be for you." Jignesh (Miami) expressed his resolve on Swamishri's word.
So Swamishri looked at the other teenagers and said, "What do you have to do?"
They all said, "We have to work according to your command."

Then he said, "All right. Thank you."
Giving them this memory, he went to sleep.

During letter writing, Roshan, a youth who stays in his service, today asked Mahant Swami Maharaj, "When you were a child, did you ever have a fight or an argument with anyone?"
"No, never. Not even once did that happen. Everyone became my friend," Swamishri said.
Overwhelmed by Swamishri's friendly nature, the youth asked further, "When you have darshan of Thakorji, what do you think about?"

Hearing this, Swamishri said with feeling, "God has been very kind to us. He has given us a grand association. I give thanks (for it). While having darshan, I keep eye contact. I have darshan with my gaze fixed. If that (eye contact) happens, the mind does not wander elsewhere."
In this way, through himself, Swamishri taught the ideal way of having darshan of God and the guru.
Today, as Mahant Swami Maharaj was sliding back on his bed to lie down, the sadhus asked, "Which world are you going to now?"
"To Akshardham..." Swamishri said as naturally as if it were his daily routine. Then, with a gesture of both hands, he said, "Here too it is the same (Akshardham), isn't it!"

Bhagwan Swaminarayan has said, "A Sadhu who understands, 'God is always present within my consciousness'... and who regards his own soul as distinct from the three bodies, gross, subtle and causal, and understands that God constantly resides within it, then God and God's abode are not even an atom's distance away from that Sant... And when one has darshan of such a Sant, one should know, 'I have had darshan of God in person...'"
Swamishri has such understanding. That is why, in his darshan, everyone feels the joy and experience of God's darshan.
